_read_this_first: This file AMENDS configs/dcs_ts_pr059_phase11.json (DCS-PR-059), which is FROZEN and is NOT edited,
and SUPERSEDES configs/dcs_ts_pr061_phase11_amendment.json (DCS-PR-061), which is also FROZEN and is
also NOT edited. Both parents are pinned by sha16 in `amendment`. An amendment is a NEW file.
WHAT CHANGED SINCE DCS-PR-061. Five of its six open BLOCKING items are now CLOSED ON MEASURED
EVIDENCE -- V8 (the smoke, slurm job 870382), V10 (the liveness schema), V11 (the arm-set
disagreement, reconciled at 84 vs 84), V12 (the disabled-hook bridge) and V13 (the analyzer's
verdict path) -- and artifacts.analyzer_exists is flipped to true. Each carries a `closed_evidence`
string naming the job id, the harness numbers and the measured values. Nothing is closed here on a
claim; every number in a `closed_evidence` string was re-observed on 2026-09-09 before the flag was
flipped.
THE ONE DECISION THIS FILE MAKES. V3 -- 'measure the between-domain SD ... ON THE CONCEPT-FREE
CHANNEL, on VALIDATION DOMAINS ONLY, and recompute MDE and power ...; if power < 0.8, return CANNOT
ANSWER WITHOUT READING TEST' -- is, in its own words, a precondition for READING TEST. The run that
MEASURES it is the `kill` stage on the VALIDATION split. V3 blocking that run is circular: it makes
the phase permanently unable to answer its own precondition. V3 is therefore SCOPED to the
TEST-reading stage, exactly as PHASE 9 (DCS-PR-060) let its Q1/A1 validation power run execute while
its checklist was still open. See decision_PR059_D8.
V3 IS NOT CLOSED. It is open until it is measured. If the measurement returns power < 0.8, the
PREREGISTERED answer is CANNOT ANSWER WITHOUT READING TEST, and that branch stays reachable.
THIS FILE DOES NOT OPEN ANY TEST-READING STAGE. `--stage family --split test` still refuses, on V3
and V16. `scripts/dcs_ts_prereg.py --for-extraction` still refuses on this file, on V3 and V16, and
that refusal is the correct state.

decision_PR059_D1.the_arithmetic: The query span is 28 rows (rel_end -28..-1), constant in 6900/6900 cell-C prompts. A dose-matched random-row control for a scope of size m needs m rows drawn from the span EXCLUDING the scope's own rows, so it needs a pool of at least m out of 28-m, i.e. m <= 14. Realised pools: S_A m=5 pool 23 OK; S_C m=1 pool 27 OK; S_F m=1 pool 27 OK; S_F2 m=1 pool 27 OK; S_D m=22 pool 6 IMPOSSIBLE; S_E m=23 pool 5 IMPOSSIBLE; S_G m=28 pool 0 IMPOSSIBLE.

options_considered.option: 1. draw the control rows from the DEMONSTRATION block instead of the query span
options_considered.rejected_because: It changes what the control controls for, and it changes the experiment. This phase's intervention is a demonstration->query attention knockout: the SOURCE keys are the demonstration block and only the DESTINATION rows vary -- `intervention.source_keys`: 'IDENTICAL in every scope: only the DESTINATION rows vary. That is what makes the family a localisation experiment rather than a dose sweep.' A control whose destinations are demonstration rows blocks demo->demo attention, which is a different causal graph at a different place in the sequence, upstream of the query entirely. It would answer 'does cutting m rows anywhere matter?' when the question is 'does cutting THESE m QUERY rows matter?'. It is also not constructible through the instrument: the declared-offset selector CONSTRAINS every offset to the row's own query span precisely so that a selector cannot cut a demonstration row and report it as a query-position result.

options_considered.option: 2. drop "excluding own rows" and allow overlap
options_considered.rejected_because: Then it is not a control. Any 23-row draw from a 28-row span shares at least 18 rows with S_E; at m=22 and m=23 the 'control' IS the scope, up to a handful of rows. Its expected effect is the scope's effect, so it cannot fail, and a control that cannot fail is a check that binds nothing. This is the repo's own 'a check that reads the same broken source' shape.

options_considered.option: 3. ACCEPT that S_D/S_E/S_G have no random-row control, DEMOTE them from primary, and rely on the other declared controls -- ADOPTED
options_considered.adopted_because: It is the only option that changes nothing about what the arms are and states the loss plainly. S_D, S_E and S_G still run, still report their full per-domain distributions, still carry the nondemo-KEY control (whose draw pool is non-demonstration KEYS and is therefore unaffected by the query span's size), and S_D vs S_E is still dose-matched to within one row by construction. What it costs is stated in `what_is_lost` and is not small.

options_considered.option: 4. redefine the primary contrast onto a smaller scope pair (S_C vs S_F, 1 row each, both controllable)
options_considered.rejected_because: It would make the phase's headline a comparison the design ITSELF predicts is uninformative. primary.negative._this_is_a_real_result already says so, before any data exist: 'A single-row null (S_C, S_F) is the EXPECTED shape and on its own is close to uninformative -- it must not be reported as "that row is not the mechanism"', citing arXiv:2605.04061's 0% single-position task transfer across all 28 layers despite 100% probing accuracy. Promoting S_C vs S_F would be choosing the contrast that SURVIVES rather than the contrast the question asks, which is subset shopping with the selection moved one level up. S_C vs S_F remains an exactly dose-matched, fully controlled REPORTED comparison -- it is simply not promoted to primary.

options_considered.option: 5. (identified here, NOT adopted, recorded for a future preregistration) control the DIFFERENCE ROW rather than the scope
options_considered.what_it_would_be: The primary contrast is a DIFFERENCE of two scopes, and what needs controlling is the ONE row by which they differ. The dose-matched control for that row is `S_D plus one random non-codeword row`: m=1 drawn from the span excluding S_D's 22 rows and excluding the codeword row -10, a pool of 5 ({-5,-4,-3,-2,-1}) and 5 distinct 1-row draws available for the 3 the design requires. That arm is 23 rows, exactly matched to S_E, and differs from it only in WHETHER THE ADDED ROW IS THE CODEWORD. It is arithmetically constructible.
options_considered.not_adopted_because: It is a NEW ARM, and the arm manifest is built by the FROZEN analyzer (scripts/dcs_ts_pr059_localisation.build_arm_manifest). Adding it means editing an analyzer that was committed before the outcome exists -- artifacts._freeze_rule: 'The analyzer is committed BEFORE the outcome exists. It is not edited to rescue an outcome. A new design is a new preregistration.' It is recorded here as the constructive path a successor preregistration should take, and it is deliberately NOT smuggled in as an amendment to this one.
options_considered.caveat_that_must_travel_with_it: the 5 rows available as substitutes are exactly S_A's scaffold rows, so the arm is only interpretable if L-N5 holds -- if the scaffold-only arm S_A moves the readout, the whole family is VOID anyway.

decision_PR059_D1.chosen: option 3, with option 5 named as the successor design
what_is_lost: PHASE 11 CANNOT ANSWER ITS OWN DECLARED PRIMARY QUESTION. 'Does removing the codeword row from an otherwise identical 23-row cut change the effect?' is asked by mandate 14.1's D-vs-E pair and it is the one comparison this design was built around. It will be REPORTED and it will carry no confirmatory weight.

The rows-versus-cells confound is NOT separated for S_D, S_E or S_G. PR-032 declared it could not separate rows from cells and the per-scope random-row control was this phase's answer to that; for the three largest scopes the answer is withdrawn. Within S_A, S_C, S_F and S_F2 it still holds.

The S_D-vs-S_E difference cannot separate 'the codeword row specifically' from 'one more row of any kind'. The two arms differ by one row of DOSE as well as by that row's IDENTITY, and those are exactly what a 23rd-random-row control would have separated. Any S_D/S_E difference is therefore an upper bound on the codeword row's contribution, never an estimate of it.

Success condition 3 is unevaluable for the three largest scopes, and success is CONJUNCTIVE, so if the only scope reaching half of S_G is S_D or S_E the phase's verdict is CANNOT ANSWER -- not a positive.

The reference scope S_G, the DENOMINATOR of every fraction this phase reports, has no random-row control either. Nothing in the manifest ever asked for one (the analyzer's build_arm_manifest gives the reference no controls), so no Holm-corrected claim rests on it; but the parent's `for every scope` clause is contradicted and the contradiction is recorded rather than read past.
what_is_NOT_lost: S_A (the scaffold null, L-N5), S_C (the codeword row), S_F (the readout row) and S_F2 all keep a fully constructible 3-draw dose-matched random-row control. The three-way comparison S_C vs S_F -- exactly dose-matched at 1 row each, both controlled -- is intact and is what the phase can still answer cleanly.
The nondemo-KEY control exists for EVERY scope regardless of size: its draw pool is non-demonstration KEYS with query_span_positions protected, so the 28-row span does not bound it.
Every scope's effect as a FRACTION of S_G, the 0.5 rule, the Holm family, S_B at p = 1.0, and both installation strata are unchanged.
decision_PR059_D1.mandate_14_justification: Mandate section 14.1 says exactly two things about dose: 'define a SMALL family such as A..F' and 'Match dose wherever the scientific comparison requires it.' It does NOT require a random-row control for every scope -- that is the parent's own tightening, and it is a good one. Where the scientific comparison requires matched dose, this decision leaves it matched: S_C vs S_F is 1 row against 1 row, and S_D vs S_E is 22 against 23 by construction. What is withdrawn is the parent's extra requirement in the three places it is arithmetically unbuildable, and the withdrawal is declared BEFORE any outcome exists. Mandate 14.1 also says 'If a further hypothesis is suggested by these results: new preregistration. No subset shopping.' -- which is why option 5 is named and not adopted, and why option 4 (promoting the contrast that survives) is refused.

NOTHING is selected in this phase -- layer, band, scope set, threshold, channel and probe are all inherited frozen -- so there is no selection for a held-out set to protect against. The 23 test domains are ALSO reported separately as a leakage-0 confirmation, and where the two disagree the smaller, cleaner one is what the claim rests on.
primary.test: group permutation at the DOMAIN level, arm-label flip within domain
primary._p_floor_rule: EVERY p IS PUBLISHED NEXT TO ITS FLOOR, 1/(n_perm+1) = 9.999e-05. On zero exceedances the report reads 'p < 9.999e-05 (= floor)', never 'p = 0'. A p AT its floor is a statement about the resolution of the design, not a measurement of the effect. R-116's own installation table has SIX p-values all at the floor and says so.
primary.secondary_test: two-sided exact sign test over domains with the tie count; its floor is 1.93e-34 at n=113 and 2.384e-07 at n=23, so the permutation floor is the binding one
primary._row_level_permutation_is_forbidden: measured false-positive rate 0.2000 on this design. It appears in no arm, no secondary and no diagnostic in this phase. A significant row-level p-value does not establish a domain-level claim (mandate section 33).

primary._largest_risk: THE CONCEPT-FREE CHANNEL IS ONLY WEAKLY ENGAGED. Median option_mass is 0.1138 -- the two scored options carry about a ninth of the next-token mass and a THIRD word is the model's actual answer ~89% of the time. So semantic_logodds is an ordering inside a residual, and a knockout can move that ordering while the model's actual output word never changes. MITIGATION, PREREGISTERED: (1) the argmax decoded answer and the full option_mass distribution are reported for every arm beside every delta, never after it; (2) an argmax-switch rate is reported as a corroborant, expected to be small and NOT required for success (mandate 10.5 item 4 says 'ideally'); (3) if median option_mass in an arm drops below the gate the arm is CANNOT ANSWER. decision_PR059_D8.the_circularity: V3 says: measure the between-domain SD of the paired knockout delta in semantic_logodds ON THE CONCEPT-FREE CHANNEL, on VALIDATION DOMAINS ONLY, and recompute MDE and power for the declared 0.5-nat effect; if power < 0.8, return CANNOT ANSWER WITHOUT READING TEST. There is no run in this design that produces that SD except the `kill` stage on the VALIDATION split -- it is the only stage that puts a knockout arm and its baseline on the concept-free channel over validation domains. In DCS-PR-061 V3 declares applies_to_stages ["kill", "family"], so that run is blocked by the item it would answer. The item can then never be closed, and the phase can never reach either of its preregistered branches -- PROCEED or CANNOT ANSWER WITHOUT READING TEST.
options_considered: 1. Mark V3 done:true because the launcher exists. REJECTED: the item is a MEASUREMENT and nothing has measured it. That is the 'published threshold never enforced' failure with the sign flipped.
2. Demote V3 to blocking:false. REJECTED: it would stop blocking the TEST read too, which is the one thing it must never stop doing.

3. Assume a value for the SD from the nearest available rows (dcssow_*, 6 domains, a different bank). REJECTED: `--u3-inventory` already returns rc=2 NOT CLOSABLE for exactly this reason -- those rows cannot form an SD for this population, and one estimate is not a stability property.
4. Scope V3 to the stage it actually gates -- the TEST-reading stage -- and make the runner RE-DERIVE that scope at launch from the population the run will actually score. ADOPTED.
5. Read TEST now and measure the SD there. REJECTED outright: that is the read V3 exists to prevent.
